forms: gen. меня́; dat. мне; instr. мной

note: «нет» is the answer "no"; «не» goes right before the word it negates: я не знаю

forms: gen. тебя́; dat. тебе́; instr. тобо́й
note: for one close person; to a stranger you say «вы»

forms: gen. чего́; dat. чему́; instr. чем; prep. чём

examples.en: That's what I was talking about.

note: pronounced «што»; as a conjunction it means "that"
where to? + acc., where? + loc.: в дом - into the house, в доме - in the house

examples.en: I never even thought about it.

note: «это» does not change: это брат, это сестра, это дети

forms: gen. его́; dat. ему́; instr. им
note: after a preposition it takes н-: у него, к нему, с ним

forms: бу́ду, бу́дешь; past был, была́, бы́ло
note: left out in the present tense: он дома, я студент

forms: gen. нас; dat. нам; instr. на́ми

examples.en: He's waiting for us outside the house.

note: «мы с братом» = my brother and I (the two of us)

forms: gen. вас; dat. вам; instr. ва́ми
note: also for one person, as a polite form; the verb is plural: вы пришли
+ instr. (with) and + gen. (from): с работы - from work

examples.en: The book is on the table.

note: where?: на заводе, на почте - at the factory, at the post office

forms: gen. её; dat. ей; instr. ей

examples.en: I've known her for a long time.

note: after a preposition it takes н-: у неё, к ней, с ней

forms: gen. их; dat. им; instr. и́ми
note: after a preposition it takes н-: у них, к ним, с ними
stress shifts: могу́ (ending), мо́жешь (stem)
in conversation it can also mean «but»

forms: gen. всего́; dat. всему́; instr. всем
note: всё = everything (neuter), все = everyone: do not mix them up

examples.en: He lives at a friend's place.
The store is next to the house.

note: у меня есть = I have (literally: by me there is)

examples.en: Will you come? No, I won't.

note: нет + gen.: нет времени - there is no time

examples.en: I don't know where he is.

note: знать a person = to be acquainted with; "to know how to" is «уметь», not знать

examples.en: I want to, but I can't.
He's not stupid, but he's lazy.

note: «но» = but; for "but rather" after a negation «а» is usually used

examples.en: My name is Ira, and yours?

note: after a negation it means "but rather": не кофе, а чай
before a vowel it becomes «об»: об этом, обо мне

forms: f. моя́; n. моё; pl. мои́
хочу́, хо́чешь, хо́чет, хоти́м; pf. захоте́ть
note: irregular: хочу́, хо́чешь, but хоти́м, хотя́т

forms: f. э́та; n. э́то; pl. э́ти; gen. э́того
note: «этот» = this; «тот» = that (the other one)

examples.en: If it rains, we'll stay home.
Could you tell me, please, where the station is?

note: perfective: to say something once; the imperfective is говорить

examples.en: I'm going to get some bread.

note: where? + instr. (behind), where to? + acc.; идти за хлебом - to go and get bread
the same for all persons: я бы, ты бы, мы бы; the verb is in the past form

forms: f. та; n. то; pl. те; gen. того́
note: тот = that (the other one); тот же - the same; тот, кто - the one who

related.en: to become thoughtful, to lose oneself in thought
to think over, to think for a while

note: думать о + loc.: думаю о тебе - I'm thinking of you

examples.en: We walked up to the house.
Toward evening it started to rain.

note: + dat.; before «мне» it becomes «ко»: ко мне. Идти к врачу - to go to the doctor
with a different subject the verb is in the past form: хочу, чтобы ты пришёл
«есть» is also "there is": у меня есть брат - I have a brother

forms: f. твоя́; n. твоё; pl. твои́

examples.en: We arrived on that very same day.

note: stresses the word before it: кто же? - who, then?

forms: f. своя́; n. своё; pl. свои́
note: refers back to the subject of the sentence: я люблю свою жену - I love my wife

examples.en: He took a key out of his pocket.

note: the opposite of «в»; the opposite of «на» is «с»: из дома, but с работы, с юга

examples.en: Would you like some more tea?

note: ещё не - not yet; ещё раз - once more

examples.en: We talked for a long time.

note: to say something once: сказать; to speak, to talk: говорить

forms: f. должна́; n. должно́; pl. должны́
note: short forms only: он должен, она должна, они должны

forms: f. вся; n. всё; pl. все; gen. всего́
note: весь день - the whole day; все - everyone, all

examples.en: This is a gift for Mom.

note: + gen.: для мамы - for Mom
colloquial; the sense depends on intonation: well, come on, so

forms: gen. кого́; dat. кому́; instr. кем; prep. ком

examples.en: I don't know who he's waiting for.

note: takes a masculine singular verb: кто пришёл?

forms: f. така́я; n. тако́е; pl. таки́е

examples.en: I need a person like that.

note: before an adjective it means "so": такой добрый - so kind
+ dat.: по городу - around town, по телефону - by phone

forms: f. кото́рая; n. кото́рое; pl. кото́рые

examples.en: Here is the man who helped me.
The movie we watched was good.

note: кото́рый час? = what time is it?
то ... то = now ... now; если ..., то = if ..., then
то́лько что = just now

forms: f. одна́; n. одно́; pl. одни́

examples.en: This is one of the best movies.

note: also means "alone": он живёт один

examples.en: There were five people in the room.

note: pl. is «лю́ди», not «человеки»; after a number: пять человек
вот points to something near, вон to something farther away
лекарство от кашля - cough medicine (literally: against a cough)

forms: f. ва́ша; n. ва́ше; pl. ва́ши

note: no nominative; вести себя - to behave

examples.en: We haven't seen each other for a long time.

note: видеть is to see (perceive); смотреть is to look at, to watch
«потому́» means "that's why"; "because" is «потому́ что»
«Как дела́?» = How are you? (literally: how are things)
уже не = no longer; ещё не = not yet
the weather (rain, sun) is «пого́да», not «вре́мя»

forms: f. на́ша; n. на́ше; pl. на́ши

note: the reply is «пожалуйста» - you're welcome
also means "grown-up": ты уже большой
«давай» + verb = let's: давай пойдём - let's go
«сейчас приду» = I'll be right there
+ dat. and infinitive: мне нужно идти - I need to go

forms: иду́, идёшь; past шёл, шла; pf. пойти́
note: идти is one direction at one time; ходи́ть is habitual or round trip

examples.en: I don't know where he is.

note: где = location, «куда» = direction: куда идёшь? - where are you going?

examples.en: This is better than I thought.

note: after a comparative: старше, чем я; чем ... тем = the ... the
pronounced «ничево»; also "not bad" and "never mind"

related.en: to get along, to fit together

note: colloquial
of time it means both "until" and "before": до войны - before the war

examples.en: I'm tired because I worked a lot.
He's sick, that's why he didn't come.

note: потому что = because; потому, поэтому = that's why

forms: f. сама́; n. само́; pl. са́ми
note: agrees with the subject: я сам, она сама́

forms: gen. дня; pl. дни, gen. pl. дней
note: after «два, три, четыре» gen. sg.: два дня

forms: f. кака́я; n. како́е; pl. каки́е

examples.en: What kind of tea do you want?

note: pl. друзья́ (stress on the ending)

forms: gen. ра́за; pl. разы́; gen. pl. раз
note: gen. pl. is раз: пять раз - five times

examples.ru: В этом [году́] я поеду в Россию.
examples.en: This year I'm going to Russia.

note: after 5 and up: пять лет, not «годов»; в году́ (stress on the ending)
does not change: её брат, её сестра, её дети

forms: пойду́, пойдёшь; past пошёл, пошла́; impf. идти́

examples.en: Tomorrow we're going to the movies.

forms: найду́, найдёшь; past нашёл, нашла́; impf. находи́ть

examples.en: He spent his whole life in the village.

note: не надо = don't, no need; мне надо = I have to

forms: дам, дашь; past дал, дала́, да́ли; impf. дава́ть
note: past: дал, дала́, да́ли (the stress moves in the feminine)

examples.en: I don't know whether he'll come.

note: follows the word being asked about: знаешь ли? - do you know?
informal «пока!» = bye; пока не = until

examples.en: Say hi to him for me.

note: informal; the formal greeting is здравствуйте, not «привет»

forms: f. друга́я; n. друго́е; pl. други́е

examples.en: Our house is not far from the sea.

note: pl. дома́ (stress on the ending)

examples.en: Do you understand what you're saying?

note: written «г», pronounced «х»: бог sounds like «бох»

forms: помогу́, помо́жешь; past помо́г, помогла́; impf. помога́ть
note: + dat.: помочь другу, not + acc.
что́-то = something; что-нибудь = anything, something or other
pl. is «де́ти», not «ребёнки»; 2 ребёнка, 5 детей
colloquial; calls attention, not a greeting

forms: смогу́, смо́жешь; past смог, смогла́; impf. мочь

examples.en: I won't be able to come.
He managed to open the door.
Will you be able to help us?

note: past «смог» often means "managed to": он смог открыть дверь
colloquial

examples.en: If you don't want to, then don't go.
I didn't understand a single word.

note: «ни» is used together with «не»: ни слова не понял - didn't understand a word
colloquial; same as «здесь»
pronounced «конешно» (чн as шн)

examples.en: I have a lot of work.
There are no free seats on the bus.
My father works as a doctor.

note: gen. отца́: the «е» drops out and the stress moves to the ending

examples.en: This is a book that is really needed.

note: мне нужен/нужна = I need; it agrees with the thing needed: мне нужна помощь

forms: возьму́, возьмёшь; past взял, взяла́; impf. брать

examples.en: He borrowed a book from me.
I can't forgive him for this.

note: «прости́те» = excuse me, pardon me (polite)

examples.en: He was killed in the war.

note: bookish; in speech: «у меня есть» = I have
pronounced «пажалуста»; also the reply to «спасибо»

examples.en: I'll be back in an hour.

note: вернуть + acc. = to give something back; -ся = to come back
pronounced «севодня» (г sounds like в)

forms: f. две; gen. двух; dat. двум; instr. двумя́

examples.en: I've lived here for two years.

note: f. «две»: две книги; after «два» gen. sg.: два дома

examples.en: How did you end up here?

note: «сюда́» = to here, «здесь» = at here: иди сюда, я здесь

examples.en: How much does the bread cost?

note: сто́ить (to cost) is not стоя́ть (to stand)

forms: пойму́, поймёшь; past по́нял, поняла́; impf. понима́ть

note: colloquial «значит» = so, then; the verb is значить

forms: приду́, придёшь; past пришёл, пришла́; impf. приходи́ть

examples.en: Tomorrow I'll come to see you.

note: past пришёл (no «й»); the infinitive is прийти
смотреть is to look or watch on purpose; видеть is to see

forms: gen. никого́; dat. никому́; instr. нике́м
note: takes a masculine verb: никто не пришёл

examples.en: I'm always glad to see you.

note: можно = it is allowed; нельзя = it is not allowed
a foreign form of address; Russian usually says господи́н

meanings: to look, to take a look

note: слышать is to hear; слушать is to listen

forms: f. пе́рвая; n. пе́рвое; pl. пе́рвые

meanings: to be going to, to intend

examples.en: I'm getting ready to go to the store.
We get together in the evening.

note: я собираюсь + inf. = I'm going to, I intend to
plural only: много денег - a lot of money

meanings: to like, to be pleasing to
note: + dat.: мне нравится кофе - I like coffee (literally: coffee is pleasing to me)
+ gen.: много воды - a lot of water, много людей - many people
often impersonal, neuter past: что случилось?

forms: acc. ру́ку; pl. ру́ки; gen. pl. рук
note: means both hand and arm: from the shoulder to the fingertips

forms: f. са́мая; n. са́мое; pl. са́мые

examples.en: He lives right in the center.

note: самый + adjective = superlative: самый большой - the biggest

meanings: to talk, to have a word
note: по- = for a short time: поговорить = to talk a little

examples.en: What will I get for this?

note: a foreign form of address; Russian says господи́н
stresses something obvious: ты ведь знал - you knew, after all
просить is to ask for something, not to ask a question (that is спрашивать)

examples.en: First I'll eat, then I'll go.
There are only five minutes left.

note: in everyday speech «машина» also means a car: ехать на машине - go by car

examples.en: The doctor is listening to the patient's chest.

note: слушать is to listen; слышать is to hear
of time it means "in": через час - in an hour
feminine in Russian: эта проблема

examples.en: There are three women in the room.

note: «жена́» means wife; a woman is «же́нщина»

examples.en: Find out when the train is.

note: мне кажется = it seems to me; + instr.: кажется умным - seems smart

examples.en: I want to see the sea.

forms: f. после́дняя; n. после́днее; pl. после́дние

examples.en: What do I need that for?

note: зачем = what for (purpose); почему = why (cause)

forms: уйду́, уйдёшь; past ушёл, ушла́; impf. уходи́ть
note: past ушёл, ушла́ (no «й»)
masculine, although it ends in -а: мой папа
also "ready, willing": я готов помочь
pl. доктора́ (stress on the ending)

forms: acc. по́ру; pl. по́ры; gen. pl. пор

examples.en: It's time for us to go.

note: нам пора идти = it's time for us to go

examples.en: I left my keys at home.
Excuse me, how do I get to the station?

note: «извини(те)» = excuse me, sorry; извиниться = to apologize

examples.en: The cat is sleeping under the table.

note: под Москвой = near Moscow (in the surrounding area)

examples.en: He has the right to vote.

note: short adjective «прав» = right, correct: он прав - he's right

examples.en: I'm ready to die for you.

note: past: у́мер, умерла́, у́мерли
after a time expression it means "ago": неделю назад - a week ago
